criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a plan test shows urgent before high, high before normal, with a dependency still ordered first even when the dependent is urgent.
criteria.evidence: plan::tests::urgent_comes_before_high_before_normal_and_a_dependency_still_comes_first passed. It asserts order [u,h,n], and [base,u,h] when the urgent item depends on the normal one.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a test shows a priority record for a queued request overrides the priority in its text; the order in plan and the priority in status change, and no new request record is written.
criteria.evidence: a_priority_record_overrides_the_priority_in_the_request_text passed. With 'Priority: low', the plan order is [other, slow] and status shows Low. After set_priority urgent, status shows Urgent and the plan order is [slow, other]. The request is equal to the stored one before, request_jobs().len()==2, and exactly one priority record has n=1. It also checks that a later record wins.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a reading test parses a ReadingOutput with an urgent reason and with null, and shows the reason reaches the recorded Reading; a speed-improving request is marked urgent with a reason and an ordinary one is not.
criteria.evidence: outputs test parses urgent_reason string and null. a_scripted_reading_with_an_urgent_reason_reaches_the_recorded_reading_and_null_does_not shows that a reason is recorded in the Reading, and that blank and null give None. a_speed_improving_request_is_read_as_urgent_with_a_reason_and_an_ordinary_one_is_not passed (fake reader).

criteria.criterion: The new CLI command appends a priority record, rejects unknown priority values and unknown or non-queued requests with a clear error; Priority::from_text parses 'Priority: urgent'; main.rs help mentions urgent and the command.
criteria.evidence: reading.rs set_priority errors with 'unknown priority "bogus"; use one of urgent, high, normal, low', uses records.resolve for unknown jobs, and bails 'job X is <state>; only a queued request can be given a priority'. All three are checked before any commit, and the test asserts head is unchanged. The plan.rs from_text test now asserts Urgent. The main.rs Priority subcommand doc and the drain help text mention urgent and `athena priority`; the help test passed.

criteria.criterion: The urgent-marking rule (makes Athena faster or cuts wasted time: failed or rejected attempts, planning stops, timeouts, redo-work retries, thrash, duplicated checks; reason required) is in outputs.rs or briefs.rs; reader.md does not grow.
criteria.evidence: The ReadingOutput.urgent_reason doc comment in outputs.rs holds the full rule. The test asserts the schema description contains every term. The diff stat shows no change to reader.md.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets: the reader set stays within 2000 tokens.

Run cargo test: a new test parses docs/decisions.md into entries and checks each has a Provenance bullet, ids are unique and ascending, and against the base commit existing entries are byte-identical with additions only at the end; it passes on the final file.
criteria.evidence: the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to passed on the final file. criteria.evidence: decisions.md has 47 insertions and 0 deletions, in one hunk after D121's last line. D122 has Case, Decision, Alternatives (a–h), Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance. CHANGELOG has an Added entry.

findings.summary: PINNED_LEN 230046 was not independently confirmed to equal the base file length
findings.evidence: The verifier role cannot run wc or cat-file. The test passing and an additions-only diff after D121 make it very likely, but if the pinned length were shorter than base, the tail of D121 would be unguarded.

findings.summary: The unknown-job error is only asserted as non-empty, not as clear
The CLI command path (stdout/json output) is not exercised end to end through the binary; only set_priority and help are
findings.evidence: The tests call athena.set_priority directly, and the binary is run only with --help.

findings.summary: The pinned hash must be advanced by hand whenever a decision is appended
findings.evidence: This is documented as a tradeoff in D122. Until the constants are raised, later appends are unguarded.

summary: The change adds Priority::Urgent above High, an `athena priority <job> <level>` command that appends an athena.priority/1 record (queued jobs only, validated levels), and a single JobRecords::priority() resolver used by both plan and status. It also adds the reader's urgent_reason field, whose urgent rule is the field's schema description in outputs.rs, so reader.md is unchanged. Finally, a decisions.rs test guards docs/decisions.md: Provenance per entry, unique ascending ids, and a pinned SHA-256 of the bytes through D121. D122 is appended after D121 with alternatives and Provenance, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry. I ran every planned targeted test (plan ordering, priority override, urgent reading, decisions guard, budgets, outputs schema) and all passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. All changed files are on the deliverables list. Only minor findings remain.
